overallNotes: Evan Michael Dorsey's arc across nearly four years (Jan 2025 - Sep 2028) tells the story of a senior procurement analyst who systematically builds a districtwide purchasing reform from scratch while managing a complex multigenerational household. His professional narrative follows a clear arc: tentative onboarding, informal cleanup assignment, formal mandate, spring pilot at three schools, summer HVAC derailment that triggers off-workflow purchasing chaos, a redesigned system with emergency exception codes, districtwide rollout, enforcement authority via title promotion (Lead Procurement Analyst for Purchasing Systems), and eventual system stabilization with near-zero audit exceptions. The personal arc runs in parallel: household coordination with wife Danielle (respiratory therapist), raising daughter Mina (preschool at start, elementary by end), and sharing a crowded split-level in Maplewood with mother-in-law Lourdes in the basement suite. Recurring themes include stress headaches tied to work pressure, a tight budget strained by preschool tuition, eldercare costs, and home safety modifications; a strong preference for structured small-scale leisure (crime fiction, local museum outings, pickup basketball, public radio, newsroom comedies); and a gradual evolution from absorbing all burden himself to setting boundaries, using employee counseling benefits, and trusting the systems he built. Key relationships: Danielle (wife and co-logistics partner), Marcus Jeffries (Mizzou friend, municipal budgeter, book and show recommender), Patrice Holcomb (assistant superintendent sponsor), Rashad Coleman (warehouse ground-truth voice), and Lourdes (mother-in-law, evolving from tension source to cooking connection). The dominant throughlines are procurement reform as a multiyear systems-building project and Evan's parallel journey toward accepting that durable structure -- not personal heroics -- is what stabilizes both a school district and a household. Current tags on all slices were generic regex output; replacement tags are specific to each slice's concrete content.
